sections.name: surveyWorkflow, resolveSurveyWorkflowStage
sections.title: The two demo stages and their lookup
sections.what: Defines the two stages with their bilingual text, related information and safe actions, plus a lookup that returns one of them from a stage name. The text states clearly that no government process has started.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed two-step map suits the demo, and the wording keeps it honest about what has happened.
sections.watch_out: An unknown stage name silently falls back to the records-ready stage rather than raising an error.

summary: Defines the two stages a demo case moves through, with plain-language text in English and Hindi.
purpose: Tells a citizen what stage their demo case is in, what it means, what information matters and what they can safely do next.
why: Likely reason: a plain stage map keeps wording and next steps in one place, and the text states that no government process has started.
how: A stage type sets the shape each stage must have: identifier, labels, explanation, relevant information, safe actions, optional next stage and caution, all in both languages. The surveyWorkflow table holds two stages, the case-created stage and the records-ready stage. The resolveSurveyWorkflowStage function takes a stage name as text and returns one of the two stages.
outputs: One stage object with its bilingual text.
risks: Any input that is not exactly the case-created label returns the records-ready stage, so a typo or unknown value shows the later stage. The lookup relies on English display text, so changing that label breaks the match.
debug: If the wrong stage appears, check the text passed in matches the English label exactly. Check that each Hindi field is filled in.
